colorPalette.title: Color Palette Generator
colorPalette.description: Automatically generate harmonious color combinations from a base color.

harmonies.title: Color Harmony
items: Complementary: Opposite on color wheel (strong contrast)
Monochromatic: Same hue with varying lightness/saturation

tips.title: Design Tips
items: Ensure sufficient contrast between background and text
Don't rely solely on color to convey information (color blindness)
Check WCAG contrast ratio guidelines for accessibility

whatIs.title: What is the Color Palette Generator?
whatIs.description: The color palette generator automatically creates harmonious color combinations from a single base color using color theory principles such as complementary, analogous, triadic, and tetradic relationships. It is ideal for web and app UI design, brand identity planning, and interior color selection. Generated colors can be copied in HEX, RGB, or HSL format.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Pick a base color using the color picker or enter a HEX code directly.
2. Select a harmony type: Complementary, Analogous, Triadic, Tetradic, or Split-Complementary.
3. Click any color in the generated palette to copy its HEX/RGB/HSL code to the clipboard.
4. Export the entire palette as a JSON object or CSS custom properties for use in your project.

items.q: What is the difference between complementary and analogous colors?
items.a: Complementary colors sit directly opposite each other on the color wheel, creating strong contrast. Analogous colors are adjacent and form a soft, natural harmony.

items.q: How can I use this for brand color selection?
items.a: Choose your primary brand color, then use split-complementary or analogous colors as accent colors. Pair with neutral tones (gray, white) to complete a consistent brand palette.

items.q: Can I check color accessibility contrast ratios here?
items.a: For WCAG contrast ratio checks between text and background colors, use the Color Converter tool which includes an accessibility checker.
